problem_statement: The VFS should provide a new function `bool vfs_iterate_mount_dirs(vfs_DIR *dir)` that enumerates mounted file systems by their root directories in a way that can be used while other mounts or unmounts occur. A caller zero-initializes `dir`, then repeatedly calls the function; each successful call must return true and leave `dir` pointing at the root directory of the next mounted file system, with `dir->mp->mount_point` giving the mount point. It must continue in mount order, skip a mount point that has been unmounted before it is reached, and still report a mount point that is mounted later in the list, including one that is remounted at the end after being unmounted. When no further mounted file system is available, it must return false so that a later call after zero-initializing `dir` starts a new enumeration from the first mounted file system, and it must not leave the enumeration holding the mount points such that they cannot be unmounted after enumeration ends.

verification.reason: The statement mostly specifies the required behaviour, but it does not make explicit that previously passed mount points may be unmounted while iteration continues, that false releases the current mount point, and that remounted already-passed mount points are reported again in the same enumeration. These can be repaired by adding observable behaviour requirements.

problems.detail: The hidden test unmounts mount points that the iterator has already passed before the enumeration returns false. The statement only says the enumeration must not hold mount points after enumeration ends, so it does not clearly require that previously passed mount points are no longer held during ongoing iteration.

The hidden test expects a mount point that was already reported, then unmounted and remounted before the end of the same enumeration, to be reported again. The statement is ambiguous about whether duplicate reporting of the same mount point in one enumeration is allowed or required.
The hidden test depends on returning false releasing the current mount point so that later unmounts and a fresh enumeration can succeed. This is implied but not explicit enough in the statement.

problem_statement_fixed: The VFS should provide a new function `bool vfs_iterate_mount_dirs(vfs_DIR *dir)` that enumerates mounted file systems by their root directories in a way that can be used while other mounts or unmounts occur. A caller zero-initializes `dir`, then repeatedly calls the function; each successful call must return true and leave `dir` pointing at the root directory of the next mounted file system, with `dir->mp->mount_point` giving the mount point. A successful call must replace the previous directory and must not keep the previously returned mount point held by the enumeration; after the iterator has moved past a mount point, that mount point must be unmountable while the enumeration is still active. It must continue in mount order, skip a mount point that has been unmounted before it is reached, and still report a mount point that is mounted later in the list, including one that is remounted at the end after being unmounted. If a mount point is unmounted and later remounted before the iterator reaches its new position, it must be reported at that new position, even if the same mount-point name already appeared earlier in the same enumeration. When no further mounted file system is available, it must return false, release the current directory so that no mount point is held by the enumeration, and allow a later call after zero-initializing `dir` to start a new enumeration from the first mounted file system; it must not leave the enumeration holding any mount points such that they cannot be unmounted after enumeration ends.
